verdicts.factCheck: I repeated the on-chain queries on 2026-11-22. On Robinhood Chain I fetched every log of ArbWasm (0x71) from block 0 to the head near block 120,983,000 in ranges of 5,000,000 blocks. There are 26 logs, all ProgramActivated, with 26 distinct code hashes, all at version 3. The first is in block 18,864,425 (timestamp 1784967900, 2026-07-25) and the last in block 78,438,208 (timestamp 1790964946, 2026-10-02). stylusVersion() is 3, expiryDays() is 365, keepaliveDays() is 31 and activationGas() is 2^64-1 on Arbitrum One, Robinhood Chain and Elysium. programTimeLeft returns 21,111,176 seconds for the oldest program 0xabce50d4038d9cfa6bc85ff8768d7b1e8149b2e5 and 27,108,774 seconds for the newest 0x3e65dfc1f7863f11ba0e12870bfb5fdf5913a34e, so the oldest record lapses near 2027-07-24. I tested the copy claim directly on Robinhood Chain. With the code of three activated programs placed at an unused address by state override, every call returned the same result as the call to the original, and ArbWasm.programVersion and programTimeLeft answered for the copy. With one byte of the code changed, the same call failed with ProgramNotActivated(). A simulated activateProgram with 30,000,000 gas reverted. A simulated codehashKeepalive for the oldest code hash from an unrelated account succeeded. On Arbitrum One the program 0x2e5d89a229cbd17efb0a731d26232f88c3746aa9, still at version 2, fails with ProgramNeedsUpgrade(2, 3). With a forwarding stub at the PoolManager address, transfer(address,uint256), balanceOf(PoolManager) and a hook selector sent to it as inner calls all returned failure, while the version 3 program 0xaff2f129d2bcba4649a54fb516be0cc78288898d answered transfer and balanceOf. Source at Nitro v3.12.4: CallProgram takes contract.CodeHash and calls getActiveProgram (arbos/programs/programs.go lines 206 to 218), which fails for version 0, for a version other than the current one and for an age above ExpiryDays (lines 559 to 579). ProgramKeepalive needs an active program of at least KeepaliveDays and has no caller check (lines 603 to 624). ArbWasm.ActivateProgram burns the stored activation gas before anything else (precompiles/ArbWasm.go lines 41 to 48). The GitHub tree page of v3.12.4 shows the go-ethereum submodule at 0e44603, and at that commit initNewContract accepts deployed code with the Stylus prefix (core/vm/evm.go lines 727 to 732), so a new contract with the bytes of an activated program can be created while activation is closed. The pause notice says that new and expired programs cannot be activated, that active ones run until they expire and that keepalive renews them. The Security Council report dates the change to 2026-10-02 and names the call ArbOwner.setWasmActivationGas(2^64 - 1). Both documents name Arbitrum One and Nova only.
verdicts.codeCheck: callHook makes a call with all gas and reverts with HookCallFailed when the call fails (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:131-137). A call that succeeds with fewer than 32 bytes or with another selector reverts with InvalidHookResponse (Hooks.sol:152-154). beforeModifyLiquidity calls the hook for a zero or negative liquidityDelta when the address has the before remove flag (Hooks.sol:203-204), and afterModifyLiquidity does so for the after remove flag (Hooks.sol:233-243). Both run inside modifyLiquidity (src/PoolManager.sol:156 and 178). The only bypass is the hook itself as caller (Hooks.sol:171-175 and 217), and a program that cannot run cannot be the caller. Permissions are bits of the address (Hooks.sol:337-339), and initialize accepts any address whose bits pass isValidHookAddress (Hooks.sol:109-127, PoolManager.sol:126). The swap and donate hooks fail the same way (Hooks.sol:255-256, 298-302, 322-323 and 332-333). For a token, take debits the caller and then calls transfer, and a failed call reverts with ERC20TransferFailed (PoolManager.sol:291-297, src/types/Currency.sol:64-86). sync and the ERC-20 branch of _settle call balanceOf and revert with it (PoolManager.sol:285 and 359, Currency.sol:94). I found no guard that changes this path. One limit on the token case: modifyLiquidity makes no token call, and mint writes a delta and a claim balance only (PoolManager.sol:322-329). A liquidity provider in a pool whose token stopped answering can still remove liquidity, mint claims for the dead token and take the other currency. What stays locked is the balance of the dead token.
verdicts.corrections: The actor and the severity stand. The actor is pool-creator because the victims must use a pool whose hook or currency the creator chose. The creator cannot bring about the lapse at will: it needs 365 days without a keepalive, which any account can pay while the record is live, or a Stylus version change by chain governance. Four additions. First, the two Arbitrum documents cover Arbitrum One and Nova. For Robinhood Chain the closed activation rests on the on-chain value of activationGas() and on the date of the last activation, and I found no statement by the chain operator. Second, a copy shares the record of its code hash. One keepalive extends the original and every copy, and a copy deployed late has only the time the original has left. Third, I checked the 26 program addresses on Robinhood Chain. None answers balanceOf(PoolManager) as a token would: 25 revert, and 0xd6cf26df204184fc9c3f2c47c36b04eb631ecf1f returns 64 bytes of hash output for any input and appears in no Initialize event as a currency between block 77,000,000 and the head. The low bits of 16 of the 26 addresses pass isValidHookAddress. The hook is not an indexed field of Initialize, so I did not establish whether a pool uses one of them, a copy, or an EVM contract that forwards to one. Fourth, the finding lists Hooks.sol:194-245 for liquidity changes. The same failure blocks swaps and donations for hooks with those flags, which the mechanism text implies and the references omit.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Lead L-203: can a call frame on a Nitro chain carry CALLVALUE that the caller's balance did not pay, through the system caller rule, deposits, retryables or unsigned parent chain messages.
clearedSpotChecks.note: I read core/vm/evm.go at fork commit 0e44603, which the tree page of Nitro v3.12.4 shows as the pinned submodule. evm.Call sets syscall to false on Arbitrum chains below Amsterdam rules (lines 274 to 279), fails with ErrInsufficientBalance when the caller cannot pay the value (lines 282 to 284) and moves the value at lines 325 to 327. CallCode runs the same balance check (lines 395 to 397). The top frame of a transaction is checked in core/state_transition.go before execution (lines 942 to 944) and then goes through evm.Call. In arbos/tx_processor.go a deposit mints to the sender and moves the value with core.Transfer and no call frame (lines 237 to 268), a retryable submission mints the deposit and moves the call value into escrow (lines 322 and 383), and a retry moves it from escrow to the sender before the ordinary call (lines 554 to 557). Stylus calls with value go through evm.Call with the acting contract as caller (arbos/programs/api.go line 186). I ran my own probe on all three endpoints: code placed at 0xfffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffe by state override makes a nested call with 1 ETH to a callee that returns CALLVALUE. With a zero balance the call fails. With 1 ETH it succeeds, the callee sees 1e18 and its balance rises by 1e18. An ordinary address gives the same two results. On the PoolManager side the native credit is msg.value (src/PoolManager.sol:352-354), settle and settleFor are the only payable entry points (PoolManager.sol:300-307), and the contract has no path that runs _settle twice in one frame. The live sequencer build v3.13.0-rc.9 is not public. The probe covers the system caller rule on it, and the consensus-v61 module root, which I read from the three rollup contracts, covers the rest for blocks that validators accept.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Leads L-153 and L-202: does a Stylus host call or a retryable redeem run caller-chosen code inside a running call with a transient storage map other than the caller's, with storage and balance writes kept.
clearedSpotChecks.note: In arbos/programs/api.go the transient host calls read and write the StateDB map under actingAddress and refuse writes in a read-only frame (lines 119 to 127), and CALL, DELEGATECALL and STATICCALL from a program go through the same EVM instance (lines 186 to 190). ArbRetryableTx.Redeem builds the retry and emits RedeemScheduled without running it (precompiles/ArbRetryableTx.go lines 50 to 125). ScheduledTxes builds the retry from that log after the outer transaction (arbos/tx_processor.go lines 924 to 956), and the block processor queues it and applies it with a new EVM as its own transaction (arbos/block_processor.go lines 435, 566 and 719). In core/state_transition.go execute calls StartTxHook at line 837, returns at once for transactions that end in the hook, and calls StateDB.Prepare at line 950 before evm.Create or evm.Call. The transient map is assigned in three places only: the constructor, Copy and Prepare (core/state/statedb.go lines 216, 800 and 1650). arbos/tx_processor.go contains no evm.Call or evm.Create, so the hooks before Prepare run no contract code, and nothing replaces the map in the middle of a transaction. A reset inside a running unlock would be the dangerous case, because it would zero the delta counter that unlock checks at src/PoolManager.sol:112. I found no such path. The PoolManager issues CALL and STATICCALL only (Currency.sol:48, 73 and 94, Hooks.sol:134), so no other code acts under its address.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Critic gap from cycle 2: repeat the special address sweep with a forwarding stub at the PoolManager address, so that each probe is an inner call whose origin is another account, for every target and for the shapes P1, P2, P3, P5 and P7.
clearedSpotChecks.note: I ran an independent sweep with my own forwarding stubs (one for CALL, one for STATICCALL) placed at the PoolManager address by state override and an unrelated sender, on all three endpoints. Shapes: 1 wei with empty calldata, zero value with empty calldata, transfer(address,uint256) with amount 1 and amount 0, and balanceOf(PoolManager) under STATICCALL. Targets: 0x64 to 0x75, 0xff, 0xa4b05, 0x01, 0x02, 0x04, 0x09, 0x0a, 0x0b, 0x100, 0xc8, 0xc9, the EIP-2935 history contract, three other Ethereum system contract addresses, the system address, the wrapped native token of each chain, USDC on Arbitrum One, USDG on Robinhood Chain, and 0x0800, 0x2222..., 0x3333... and 0x5555... on Elysium. Every ArbOS precompile address with code fails on every shape. 0x01, 0x6a, 0x75, 0xc9, 0x100 and the addresses without code succeed with empty return data, which makes a take of that currency id a debit with no movement. 0x02 and 0x04 return data whose first word is not 1, so the transfer check at src/types/Currency.sol:64-74 rejects them. The history contract reverts on every shape. The wrapped token accepts value and answers transfer and balanceOf, and its totalSupply() equals its native balance to the wei on all three chains (123,108.08 ETH, 34,632.55 ETH and 54,716.71 HYPE), so the exchange is one for one. USDG rejects native value and answers transfer and balanceOf. In every accepting case the caller's delta is written before the call (PoolManager.sol:294-295). My sweep did not repeat the EntryPoints, the routers, the gateways or the hook selectors, and like the original it does not cover application contracts.

clearedSpotChecks.check: A2 and A5 for USDG on Robinhood Chain, which pays claimable rewards: can an ordinary account raise balanceOf(PoolManager) without a transfer, enrol the PoolManager, or earn rewards with USDG borrowed from the PoolManager inside one transaction. The PoolManager holds 16.83M USDG.
clearedSpotChecks.note: Extra check, because the PoolManager held about 17.0M USDG during my queries. On chain: payoutGroupIdOf(PoolManager) is 0, availableRewardsOf(PoolManager) is 0, getPendingRegistration(PoolManager) is empty, isPartnerSignedRegistrationsEnabled() is false and globalTransferSettings() returns 1771891200, 86400, false, 0 and false. In PayoutGroupFacet.sol of the Paxos repository the three ways into a payout group are registrarRegisterRewardAddress (registrar role, line 346), registerRewardAddress (the switch for partner signed registration must be on, the caller must be the claimer or manager, and SignatureChecker must accept a signature of the account, lines 666 to 700) and proposeRegisterRewardAddress followed by acceptRegisterRewardAddress called by the account itself (lines 422 to 471). The PoolManager emits only transfer(address,uint256), balanceOf(address), unlockCallback to its caller, the IHooks selectors and empty calldata, and it has no isValidSignature function and no fallback. The USDG address ends in 0xd168, whose low 14 bits set the before swap return flag without the before swap flag, so isValidHookAddress rejects it (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:111). An ordinary account therefore cannot enrol the PoolManager. Like the research, I matched the deployed token to the repository by selectors and view results and did not compare bytecode.
